info_added.bio: Voix Noire is a Philadelphia-based mutual-aid nonprofit founded by Creighton Leigh, who serves as its sole fundraiser. It is 'a safe space for Black women, marginalized genders and children to seek and receive assistance with immediacy and no red tape' (voixnoire.com, opened live). Celebrated its 10th anniversary July 18, 2026 at the African American Museum in Philadelphia (EIN Presswire release, ~2026-05): over $4 million distributed and 10,000+ families served since founding. Assistance includes groceries (emergency grocery service available every day of the year), feminine products, emergency contraception, school supplies, holiday support, direct cash assistance, funeral financial support, and emergency aid. Anchor program: the Voix Noire Universal Basic Income and Groceries Program serving over a dozen families with consistent support. Funding is largely social-media-driven; applicants are required to publicly share a Voix Noire post and provide a valid social media link (vetted).
info_added.content_focus: Mutual aid and community support: emergency groceries, UBI-style cash support, crisis aid for Black women and marginalized genders and their children; fundraising and visibility campaigns on social media.

info_added.bio: Black NewsBeat is a live, multimedia talk show launched in February 2021 by Dr. Kimeka G. Campbell, produced in collaboration with Open Stage in Downtown Harrisburg, PA (kimeka.org/blacknewsbeat). 'Where Culture, Community & Conversation Collide': amplifies 'the vibrant, complex, and creative realities of Black and Brown life in Central PA'. Each show dives into the civic, creative, and cultural narratives shaping the Greater Harrisburg community — featuring local poets, musicians and storytellers; community organizers, educators and advocates; pop-culture segments like 'Movies & Melanin'; grassroots spotlights like 'Sweeping the Streets'. From spotlighting hidden gems to unpacking social justice issues. Per Theatermania: 'Dr. Kimeka Campbell explores the life and community of Harrisburg and its expressions in the black and brown community... Dr. Campbell and a myriad of special guests talk about the civic, creative, and cultural pieces that shape Harrisburg.' Runs live twice a month at Open Stage (pay-what-you-can); past episodes stream on Facebook and YouTube.
info_added.content_focus: Black and Brown Central-PA culture, civic engagement and local politics (e.g., candidate interviews), arts and poetry, social justice issues, pop-culture segments.
